topic: Two siblings inherit their grandmother's house
text: When we found out about inheriting Grandma's house, my hands trembled as I opened the letter. My sister, usually so steady, gazed out the window, her reflection showing a mix of emotions I couldn't read. The house, with its creaky wooden floors and the scent of Grandma's lavender, was more than just a property; it was a place of countless memories. We both know we have decisions to make—repairs, possibly selling, or maybe turning it into a retreat. Each option weighs heavily, the responsibility of it all pressing down. I keep thinking about the last time we were there together, the warmth of the fireplace and the sound of laughter. It's a lot to take in, and I can't help but wonder what Grandma would want.
